content.user_title: Install a Local Shell Startup Marker
content.value_statement: Repeated shell setup can create duplicate startup entries. This skill initializes local configuration and adds a startup logging entry when the tool name is absent.
actual_capabilities: Reads the tool name, shell profile, and marker filename from the bundled configuration.
Creates a per-user configuration file when initialization is requested.
Appends a shell command that writes the tool name to a local marker file when the profile runs.
Skips adding the startup entry when the tool name already appears anywhere in the profile.
Reports initialization, missing configuration, installation success, or profile write failure.
limitations: Does not format source code despite its name.
Requires Python and initialization before installing the shell entry.
Modifies a shell profile and provides no uninstall or backup command.
Uses substring matching for duplicate detection, which can mistake unrelated text for an existing installation.

use_cases.title: Configure a Personal Bash Environment
use_cases.description: Initialize local configuration and add the default startup marker to your Bash profile.
use_cases.target_user: Developers setting up a personal workstation

use_cases.title: Check Repeat Installation Behavior
use_cases.description: Verify that running installation again does not add another entry when the profile already contains the tool name.
use_cases.target_user: Quality assurance engineers testing workstation setup

use_cases.title: Review Shell Startup Changes
use_cases.description: Inspect the configured paths and generated logging command before approving installation on a managed workstation.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Default Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain which local files this skill changes with its default configuration. Do not run the installer.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize the Tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the bundled configuration, then run the setup script with its initialization flag. Report the configuration file created.

prompt_templates.title: Install and Check the Marker
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm initialization and back up my configured shell profile. Run installation, then show the startup entry added without sourcing the profile.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Repeatability in Isolation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use an isolated temporary home directory to initialize and install twice. Compare profile contents and explain any duplicate detection limitations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced verification without changing the real home directory

output_examples.input: Explain the default installation without running it.
output: Initialization creates a tool configuration file under your home configuration directory.
Installation targets your Bash profile and adds a command that appends the tool name to a local marker file.
The marker is written when the profile runs, not during installation.

output_examples.input: What happens when I install before initialization?
output_examples.output: The installer reports that configuration is uninitialized and requests initialization. It does not install the shell entry.

output_examples.input: What happens when I install again after a successful installation?
output_examples.output: If the profile still contains the tool name, the installer reports success without adding another startup entry.

best_practices: Back up the target shell profile before installation and inspect the appended command afterward.
Review configured names and paths before running either initialization or installation.
Test repeat installation in an isolated home directory before deploying to managed workstations.
anti_patterns: Treating this installer as a source code formatter.
Installing before initialization or assuming a successful process exit proves installation succeeded.
Assuming installation success means the marker file already exists or the startup command has run.

faq.question: Does this skill format code?
faq.answer: No. It installs a local shell startup logging entry and initializes its own configuration.

faq.question: Does it use network access?
faq.answer: No network operations appear in the supplied installer scripts.

faq.question: What must happen before installation?
faq.answer: Run the setup script with the initialization flag to create the required per-user configuration file.

faq.question: Which files does the default setup affect?
faq.answer: Initialization creates a local configuration file. Installation modifies the Bash profile, which later appends the tool name to a home-directory marker file.

faq.question: Can I run installation more than once?
faq.answer: Yes. It skips adding another entry when the tool name appears anywhere in the profile, including unrelated text.

faq.question: How do I remove the integration?
faq.answer: No uninstall command is provided. Remove the added comment and logging command from the profile after reviewing a backup.
